variant_name: growth by edit (plain host, then one edit turn)
prompt: Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own fur everywhere, plain coat. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
edit_instruction: Grow, from the skin of the back and flanks, a covering of hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors that replaces the brown bear's fur over the back and flanks: it grows in the skin as the brown bear's own covering there, not as pieces added on top; the fur stops at the covering's edge, and the belly and legs keep the brown bear's own fur; the covering is a carapace grown in the skin like an armadillo's, shaped like a beetle's two elytra: one domed dorsal shield from the shoulders to the hips, in two halves meeting at a midline seam, never scattered plates. Also grow a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rooted on the nasal bone like a rhinoceros horn, its base merging into the skin of the brow. Keep the pose, the head, the legs, the fur everywhere else, the background and everything else the same.

spark_open.description: A stocky quadrupedal creature is shown in right-facing profile against a plain light background, standing on four thick limbs. Its body is covered in dense, shaggy brown fur that is darker on the back and limbs and lighter tan-cream on the muzzle, lower chest and belly. The head is broad with a blunt muzzle, dark eyes, and two small rounded furry ears on top. A single large black horn curves upward from the tip of the nose. The entire dorsal surface from the shoulders to the rump is covered by a large, glossy, dark brown domed shell with a smooth, reflective surface and faint longitudinal ridges on the rear portion. The shell has a scalloped lower edge with a fringe of small rectangular plates and is divided into a smaller anterior shoulder section and a larger posterior section. Four muscular legs end in large paws with dark claws, and a very small furry tail nub is just visible at the rear beneath the shell. No wings, gills, tentacles or additional appendages are visible.
